newsitem.title: FRANCE: France expels planeload of Moroccans.
newsitem.headline: France expels planeload of Moroccans.

text.p: France has sent home 55 Moroccans who entered French territory illegally or committed criminal offences here, the Interior Ministry said on Friday.
A specially chartered airliner left Paris late on Thursday for Casablanca, with a stopover in southern France to pick up 33 of the 55 tapped for expulsion, a ministry statement said.
Twenty-two of them were expelled after completing prison terms, mainly for drug trafficking or robberies committed with violence, it added.
The expulsion exercise was the 38th of its kind since Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre took office in June, 1995.
Most of the ejections have been to West and Central African countries as well as to Romania, all countries of origin for many of France's illegal immigrants.
The last such expulsion, on February 27 to Bamako, Mali, was marked by violence when several dozen of those being sent home attacked the flight crew and guards aboard the aircraft.
Several French policemen were seriously injured in the attack, which took place after the plane landed in Bamako, and the aircraft was heavily damaged when the passengers tried to set it ablaze.
Group expulsions have been denounced by civil libertarians as racist and undemocratic but opinion polls show they enjoy wide support among the French public.
The Interior Ministry said the total number of illegal immigrants expelled from France under Debre's tenure, including those expelled by sea or rail, was just over 23,000.
France's senate on Thursday approved a new draft bill to tighten loopholes im immigration laws despite significant protests by left-wing groups.
